Publication date: 28 July 2026 (metadata indicated "published 5 hours ago" at time of search).

IFS response to the government's announcement of technical pathways in schools from age 14 (tailored to local industries, combining skills training with practical work experience):
- Notes a mismatch for many young people in England between training received and work they go on to do; number of graduate jobs has not kept pace with the expansion of higher education in many places.
- England has the highest level of overqualification among OECD countries: 37% of workers overqualified for their jobs in 2022, vs an OECD average of 23%.
- Countries with strong vocational pathways linked to local employers (Germany, the Netherlands) have achieved lower field-of-study mismatch.
